To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a recombinantly engineered 10th Type III domain of human fibronectin scaffold-ligand (FN3VEGFR-2) was successfully conjugated to a commercially available ultrasound contrast agent, and that this new molecularly targeted contrast agent can be used for ultrasound molecular imaging of the VEGFR-2 on breast cancer vasculature in a mouse model of breast cancer.
MBs coupled with a recombinant engineered fibronectin scaffold ligand to VEGFR-2 can be used as a targeted contrast ultrasound agent to image the breast cancer neovascularture.
a novel class of targeted MBs using engineered FN3-scaffolding ligand for VEGFR2 can be designed and produced in a cost efficient manner for use in USMI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel class of molecularly-targeted contrast agents for USMI of the breast cancer neovascularture using FN3-scaffold ligands.
the development and evaluation of novel FN3-scaffold based MBs as a novel class of targeted contrast agents for USMI of VEGFR2.
the development and evaluation of a new class of targeted contrast agents for USMI of the cancer vasculature.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FN3 scaffolds represent a novel, promising, and cost-effective class of molecular imaging ligands for USMI of cancer.
the FN3 scaffold ligands have potential to be used for molecular ultrasound imaging of breast cancer.
FN3-scaffolding ligands are promising for molecularly-targeted contrast ultrasound imaging.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of FN3-scaffold ligands coupled to MBs can be used to target the VEGFR2 receptor in the breast cancer neovasculatures and may be useful for molecular imaging of other angiogenic targets.
the FN3-scaffold can be engineered to target VEGFR2 in vivo and can be used as a novel class of ligands for targeted contrast ultrasound imaging of breast cancer.
we have developed a novel class of MBs that are targeted to VEGFR-2 using a recombinantly engineered FN3-scaffold ligand.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FN3-scaffolding can be used to develop a novel class of MBs with potential for clinical translation.
engineered FN3VEGFR scaffolds are a promising class of ligands to be used for the molecular imaging of VEGFR2 expression in breast cancer using USMI.
engineered FN3-scaffolding ligands are potentially useful for the design of targeted MBs for molecular imaging with ultrasound of breast cancer neo-vasculature.
